headword: {焦点|しょうてん}を{絞|しぼ}る
gloss: to focus; to narrow down the focus

definitions.gloss: to focus; to narrow down the focus; to zero in on
definitions.explanation: To concentrate attention or discussion on a specific point or topic, narrowing from a broader scope. Used in discussions, research, investigations, and presentations.

examples.japanese: {議論|ぎろん}の{焦点|しょうてん}を{絞|しぼ}る。
examples.english: To narrow down the focus of the discussion.

examples.japanese: {調査|ちょうさ}の{焦点|しょうてん}を{絞|しぼ}って{効率|こうりつ}を{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: We improved efficiency by narrowing the focus of the investigation.

examples.japanese: テーマが{広|ひろ}すぎるので、もう{少|すこ}し{焦点|しょうてん}を{絞|しぼ}ったほうがいいでしょう。
examples.english: The topic is too broad, so it would be better to narrow the focus a bit more.

notes:
USAGE:
Common in academic, business, and journalistic contexts. The metaphor comes from optics — adjusting a lens to bring a subject into sharp focus.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {議論|ぎろん}の{焦点|しょうてん}を{絞|しぼ}る (to focus the discussion)
- {調査|ちょうさ}の{焦点|しょうてん}を{絞|しぼ}る (to narrow the investigation)
- {焦点|しょうてん}を{絞|しぼ}って{取|と}り{組|く}む (to work on something with a focused approach)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {焦点|しょうてん}を{当|あ}てる: to focus on — emphasizes directing attention, while {絞|しぼ}る emphasizes narrowing from a broader scope
